## Report

**MANDATORY FIRST ACTION verified:** cwd resolved to `.worktrees/engine-lane`, not the main repo — isolation confirmed before any edit. Did not `git add`/`commit`/`push` per instructions.

**Note on `npm test` / `check:ship` exit codes:** this worktree has multiple fixer bundles running concurrently, uncommitted, side by side (`git status` shows in-flight edits to `job-manager.js`, `quota.js`, `CUSTODY.md`, `scripts/checks/verified-by-resolver.js`, `custody-claim-lint.test.js`, etc. — none of these are files I touched, all explicitly out of my scope). Running the *whole* suite mid-flight of other bundles' work is noisy (counts even grew 233→243 between runs) and produced transient/non-transient failures **entirely attributable to those other files**. I isolated my own scope repeatedly (`test/entry-bootstrap.test.js`, `test/driver.test.js`, `test/custody-static.test.js`, `test/mcp-surface.test.js`, `test/permission.test.js`, `test/branding.test.js`) and it is **green every time**, and I confirmed the extra full-suite reds by diffing the offending files against HEAD (large uncommitted rewrites by other agents, not me).

### A1–A7, each with CLASS/INSTANCE

- **A1 (bootstrap restructure)** — **CLASS.** Both entries now statically import exactly one specifier (`./bootstrap.js` / `../src/bootstrap.js`), reach everything else via `await import(...)` issued only after `initCredentialCustody()` runs. This closes the ordering-claim-vs-ESM-hoisting defect as a class, not per-file — the mechanism (single static import + dynamic rest) generalizes to any future entry point, and `bootstrap.js`'s own header states why a shared file was chosen (one definition of the invariant, not two maintained in parallel).
- **A2 (standing single-import test)** — **CLASS.** `test/entry-bootstrap.test.js` asserts `extractStaticImportSpecifiers(source).length === 1` for both entries, generically (loops over `ENTRY_POINTS`), so a third entry point added later is covered by extending that array, not writing new logic.
- **A3 (transitive closure)** — **CLASS**, with a **named residual**: `walkStaticClosure` only follows *relative* specifiers recursively; a bare/`node:` specifier is still counted in a file's own list (so `env-scrub.js` growing a `node:fs` import still fails A3 — proven, see mutant table), but the walker cannot recurse *into* `node_modules` packages if `bootstrap.js`'s specifier list ever grew a non-relative entry — not a gap today (it doesn't), but the ceiling is real and stated in the file's own doc comment.
- **A4 (mutant proof)** — **INSTANCE**, by nature (each lever is a one-off manual proof). All three levers executed by hand this session (see table below), each observed RED, each reverted immediately after.
- **A5 (three claim surfaces)** — **CLASS.** Fixed `src/server-entry.js`, `driver/host-free-driver.js`, and this fix's own new test-assertion text (`test/entry-bootstrap.test.js`'s A5/A6 tests assert absence of the old wording and presence of the re-derived one for both files, generically). **Named residual:** `test/env-scrub.test.js`'s line-541 "mutant-proof lever exists" test still repeats the pre-restructure assumption (it textually requires `from "node:readline"` to exist in `server-entry.js`) — that file is explicitly forbidden to me (`src/env-scrub.js` and all `test/env-scrub.test.js` content are another bundle's scope, running after mine). This is the one known, documented, out-of-scope collateral failure — flagged below.
- **A6 (re-derived sentence)** — **INSTANCE** (a single sentence, verified true by the closure test, not merely restated): `initCredentialCustody() runs before any other module in this package's graph evaluates.` — present verbatim in both entries' headers, and asserted by A2/A3's own closure math, not just claimed in prose.
- **A7 (driver `ok` + spawn error handler)** — **CLASS.** `computeDriverOk` is now a pure, exported, unit-tested function requiring `status.outcome === "success" && !status.error`, closing "completion ≠ success" for every future caller of the driver, not just this run. The `child.on("error", ...)` handler is a general convention already used by `ship-set.js` against the same wrapper — now also present here.

### Bootstrap shape & why

`src/bootstrap.js` re-exports `initCredentialCustody`/`CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES` from `./env-scrub.js` and nothing else — a single shared file both entries import, rather than each importing `env-scrub.js` directly. Chosen because the "exactly one static import" invariant is then defined **once** and both A2/A3 tests assert against one shared target, instead of maintaining two independently-verified copies of the same rule (same anti-duplication discipline `test/custody-static.test.js` already applies to P1/P2/P4).

### Re-derived sentence (A6), verbatim

> `initCredentialCustody() runs before any other module in this package's graph evaluates.`

### A3's transitive closure computation & ceiling

`walkStaticClosure(entryAbsPath)` recursively extracts every static `import`/`export...from` specifier (regex-based, self-tested to reject dynamic `import()` and ordinary `export const x = "string"` false positives), resolves relative specifiers to files, and recurses. Two assertions per entry: (a) `env-scrub.js`'s own specifier list is `[]` — catches *any* static import there, including `node:` builtins, which "still resolve" (a builtin's own module body evaluates too, so it would also run ahead of the scrub); (b) the full closure membership is bounded to exactly `{entry, bootstrap.js, env-scrub.js}`. **Ceiling:** only relative specifiers are recursed into — a bare/npm specifier appearing anywhere in the closure is caught as "a real static import exists" (fails the length/closure checks) but not walked further; not exercised today since none of the three files in the closure has one.

### A7: new `ok` conjunction & env-hook ruling

```js
Boolean(targetRepoUnchanged) && Boolean(status) && status.outcome === "success" && !status.error && allToolsPresent
```
Extracted as `export function computeDriverOk({ targetRepoUnchanged, status, toolNames })`, unit-tested directly (7 new tests in `driver.test.js`, incl. the exact pre-fix defect: DONE-with-error and cancelled now both correctly report `false`).

**Ruling on `VLAD_DRIVER_TEST_FORCE_*` env hooks: keep them, do not retire.** They exercise a different layer (the real CLI subprocess's exit-code wiring — env var → forced value → `computeDriverOk` → `process.exit`), which the new pure-function unit tests don't cover (those only prove the function's logic, not that the CLI wiring around it is correct). Both layers are now tested; neither is redundant with the other.

Real output tails pasted above/below for each (`node --test test/entry-bootstrap.test.js` / `test/driver.test.js`). `git diff -- engine/src/env-scrub.js` is empty (byte-identical restore, read-only file honored).

### Things wrong in the brief / verified premises

1. **Verified true:** `env-scrub.js` genuinely has zero static imports — read the full file; β's ruling premise holds.
2. **Real conflict, not fixable within my scope:** the brief's DoD item 4 ("`npm test` → 0 failures") cannot be simultaneously satisfied with the forbidden-file list. `test/env-scrub.test.js`'s "mutant-proof lever exists and is inspectable" test (line 541, **not in my file scope**) does a raw textual check that `src/server-entry.js` contains `from "node:readline"` and that `initCredentialCustody(...)` precedes it — this is precisely the pre-restructure shape (multiple static imports) that A1 requires removing. **Any correct implementation of A1 breaks this specific assertion**, regardless of shape chosen (direct or bootstrap.js). This is now the **sole remaining failure in the whole suite attributable to my change** (232/233 in an isolated run). It needs a one-line fix in that forbidden file (assert the file imports from `./bootstrap.js` and calls the scrub as its first statement, drop the `node:readline` ordering check) — flagging for whoever owns `env-scrub.js`/its tests next, per the brief's own note that a later bundle owns that file.
